newsitem.title: FRANCE: France convicts six in controversial Basque trial.
newsitem.headline: France convicts six in controversial Basque trial.

text.p: A Paris court convicted three Spaniards, a French couple and a Chilean on Friday for illegal activities in support of Spanish Basque separatist group ETA.

The proceedings ended a high-profile court case which saw 32-year-old Idoia "The Tigress" Lopez Riano, sentenced on Thursday to serve five years in France before she is extradited to face 23 ETA murder charges in Spain.

In Friday's rulings, Julian "Pototo" Achurra Egurrola, logistics chief of the ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom), and ETA member Inaki Bilbao Beaskoetxea were sentenced to three years prison, while Rosario Pikabea Ugalde was sentenced to five years for conspiracy.
A couple from Brittany in northwestern France, Marie-Helene Leroux and Vincent Louet, were given suspended eight-year jail sentences for hiding Basque guerrillas in their home.
Chilean Bernardo Mella Duran was sentenced to the time he had already served in prison while in preventive detention for helping ETA activists.

The convictions were the culmination of a controversial trial in France of 16 Basque separatists and ETA sympathisers. ETA has killed 800 people since starting a drive for Basque independence a quarter-century ago.
The trial generated an emotional response, particularly in Brittany, which has its own separatist movement, and in the French Basque country along the southern border with Spain.

Pro-Basque protesters held a vigil outside the court in central Paris during the trial, accusing France of staging a political trial and arguing that many of the defendants had done nothing more than provide legal assistance to ETA.
Also convicted on Thursday was Lopez Riano's French former companion Olivier Lamotte who was carrying her pistol when the two were detained in Aix-en-Provence, southern France, in August 1994.
Lamotte was convicted of criminal conspiracy and sentenced to two years in prison.
